key_insight: Constraint-aware reinforcement learning reduces battery sizing requirements for PV ramp-rate smoothing while maintaining grid-code compliance.
engineering_relevance: Co-designing battery capacity and control can reduce storage requirements for managing rapid solar-power fluctuations.
method: Learn a causal state-feedback policy from historical PV data without requiring forecasts during deployment.
Restrict actions using a feasibility interval incorporating ramp-rate, converter-power, and state-of-charge constraints.
Compare against a full-horizon input-convex neural network optimization benchmark for minimum achievable battery requirements.
evidence_signal: Across three real-world PV datasets at a 10%/min ramp-rate limit, CARL reduced peak battery power by 8.7–10.4% and energy capacity by 47.5–62.6% relative to conventional ramp-rate control.
watch_item: Performance under PV conditions beyond the evaluated datasets remains uncertain; this study addresses PV integration and battery control, not perovskite cell materials.
paper_title: Battery Energy Storage Sizing in PV Ramp-Rate Smoothing using Constraint-Aware Reinforcement Learning-Based Controller
